brief: Design an interface for a "Memory Decay Calendar" where users document significant life moments, but each entry literally fades and distorts over time based on how human memory actually works—recent e

dominant_strengths: The extreme negative space could metaphorically suggest forgotten memory, though almost certainly unintentional given the lack of any other content
The single white dot has high contrast against black, technically legible as a focal point
dominant_weaknesses: The artifact is effectively empty—no typography, no calendar grid, no entries, no decay system, no UI affordances of any kind
Zero evidence of the brief's core mechanic: fading entries, time-based distortion, or memory documentation interface
No information architecture, no interaction model, no visual hierarchy beyond a lone dot in the corner
fix_priorities: Build an actual calendar surface with entry cells that visualize age via blur, opacity, and typographic distortion
Establish a typographic system where recent entries are crisp and older ones literally degrade in legibility
Introduce a temporal color/luminance gradient so decay is felt at a glance, not just read
Add interaction states for revisiting, reinforcing, or losing memories to make the metaphor behavioral
rationale.norman_balance: All three Norman layers collapse: nothing visceral to feel, nothing behavioral to operate, and only an accidental reflective reading of 'void as forgetting.'
rationale.intent_fit: The design fails the brief almost entirely—a black canvas with one white dot does not constitute a memory decay calendar interface.
